Our People Make the Difference! The Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland is seeking innovative thinkers with vision to build the framework that will carry the Bank into the future.

Follow us on LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, and our YouTube channel – Cleveland Fed

This position requires access to confidential supervisory information and/or FOMC information, which is limited to "Protected Individuals" as defined in the U.S. federal immigration law. Protected Individuals include, but are not limited to, U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, and U.S. permanent residents who either are not yet eligible to apply for naturalization or who have applied for naturalization within the requisite timeframe.

In addition, all candidates must undergo an enhanced background check and comply with all applicable information handling rules, and all non-U.S. citizens must sign a declaration of intent to become a U.S. citizen and pursue a path to citizenship.

The Research Department conducts policy analysis, produces academic research, and provides long-term strategic thinking on issues related to monetary policy, the national economy, and the region. Research Analysts contribute to the Research Department by: (i) supporting the research of the Bank’s economists, (ii) contributing to Bank publications, (iii) maintaining indicators on the Bank’s website, and (iv) supporting policy briefings for the Bank’s President before meetings of the Federal Open Market Committee.

The Cleveland Fed seeks Research Analysts for positions that start in the summer of 2027. During their time at the Bank, Research Analysts develop their knowledge of new areas of economics, develop their data analysis and programming skills, participate in the policy process, and work one-on-one with the Bank’s economists to conduct research that can lead to co-authored papers for Bank and external academic publications. These experiences make the Research Analyst position ideal for someone considering a Ph.D. in economics or finance. Research Analysts typically work at the Bank for 2 or 3 years.

Job Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree (completed by the summer of 2027) with emphasis in economics or a closely related field, such as finance, mathematics, statistics, or computer science; knowledge of monetary policy and macroeconomics preferred.
Working knowledge of econometrics and statistics packages, such as Stata, Matlab, R, or Python.
Prior research experience in economics and a strong mathematics background strongly preferred
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Conducts directed research that contributes to internal publications, external publications, policy advising, and outreach.
Collects and analyzes data, performs statistical and econometric analyses, writes computer programs, and conducts literature reviews.
Maintains indicators on the Bank's external website

Resume
Transcript
Writing sample (related to economics or finance)

Applications will be considered on a rolling basis, but interested individuals are strongly encouraged to apply no later than October 10th, 2026.

The expected starting salary range for the Research Analyst is $72,000
annually.
Final salary and offer will be determined by the applicant’s background, experience, skills, internal equity, and market data.

Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.

So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.

Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
The Role
As AI Legal Program Manager, you will play a key role in navigating the legal and regulatory landscape of Block's artificial intelligence initiatives. You will partner with legal, engineering, product, and compliance teams to develop frameworks that enable responsible AI innovation while ensuring regulatory compliance and risk management across our AI products and services.
You will:
Drive the development and implementation of AI legal and compliance frameworks, including policies for model development, deployment, and monitoring that align with emerging AI regulations and industry standards.
Participate in cross-functional reviews of AI project initiatives to identify legal risks and opportunities, ensuring compliance with regulations while enabling innovation.
Develop and maintain AI governance documentation, including model cards, algorithmic impact assessments, training data compliance records, and legal risk assessments.
Partner with engineering teams to implement legally compliant AI development practices, including requirements for transparency, fairness, and accountability.
Create and maintain processes for AI incident response, model monitoring, and legal compliance validation.
Build scalable processes for AI legal reviews across various stakeholders.

You have:
5+ years of directly related experience in technical program management, with at least 2 years focused on AI/ML initiatives in a technology-driven environment.
Strong understanding of emerging AI regulations (EU AI Act, state AI laws, etc.) and their practical implementation.
Experience developing legal frameworks for AI governance and responsible AI development.
Track record of partnering with technical teams to implement legal requirements in AI systems.
Understanding of IP considerations in AI development, including training data rights, model ownership, and output licensing.
Experience with AI risk assessment methodologies and mitigation strategies.
Strong project management skills with experience leading cross-functional initiatives.

Experience with large language models (LLMs) and generative AI legal considerations
Background in open source software licensing and AI model licensing
Familiarity with AI ethics frameworks and algorithmic fairness principles
Experience with AI procurement and vendor assessment

jobs.title: HR Risk Operations Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Description

The HR Risk Operations Project Manager is responsible for leading complex HR risk, compliance, and operational programs from strategy through execution. This role partners closely with People Experience, Legal, Compliance, HRIS, Payroll, Finance, and business stakeholders to translate regulatory requirements, policy priorities, and operational risks into practical programs, standard operating procedures, tools, controls, reporting, and stakeholder guidance. The Manager serves as a consultative resource on employment policy and HR compliance matters, providing clear recommendations, drafting policy-related materials, and supporting consistent, defensible decision-making across the organization.

This role requires strong project and program management discipline, including the ability to develop project plans, manage timelines, coordinate cross-functional workstreams, identify dependencies and risks, and drive deliverables to completion in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. The ideal candidate will bring strong data analytics capabilities, including experience analyzing workforce data, identifying trends and risk indicators, building dashboards or tracking tools, and translating data into executive-ready insights and recommendations.

The HR Risk Operations Project Manager serves as a key member of the People & Culture team in support of firm-wide goals and objectives. This role will report to the Associate Director of HR Risk Operations.

Key responsibilities:

HR Regulatory Program Management

Lead complex HR risk, compliance, and operational programs from planning through execution, including project plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and deliverables.
Translate legal, regulatory, and business requirements into scalable HR processes, controls, communications, training materials, and stakeholder guidance.
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams by aligning stakeholders, clarifying roles and responsibilities, documenting decisions, and ensuring timely follow-through.
Manage large-scale HR programs supporting multinational firms on the Grant Thornton platform, integrations, and business optimization initiatives.
Support firmwide compliance initiatives, including workforce analysis, Respect in the Workplace training, compliance questionnaires, and other high-priority or confidential projects in partnership with P&C and Legal.
Oversee the firmwide Affirmative Action program, including OFCCP audit response, vendor management, reporting, and program governance.

HR Risk Operations

Partner with Global HR teams to strengthen HR compliance controls and risk frameworks aligned with firm risk appetite.
Ensure HR risk monitoring frameworks remain effective, scalable, and responsive to regulatory changes and business needs.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures, research summaries, and guidance materials related to HR risk operations and emerging trends.
Lead HR risk management priorities and develop practical short- and long-term solutions for complex business challenges.
Serve as an escalation point for client-related onboarding, background investigation matters, and contract review.
Collaborate with ICS functions, including Finance and Payroll, to improve operational consistency and advance risk management priorities.
Provide day-to-day work direction to global data analytics team members supporting HR risk operations.

Policy Governance

Own the development, implementation, maintenance, and governance of employment policies.
Serve as a policy consultation resource for People Experience, Legal, Compliance, HRIS, Payroll, Finance, and business stakeholders.
Provide practical guidance on employment policy interpretation, process application, and risk mitigation.
Partner with Legal and Compliance to align policies with global requirements and firm standards.
Drive policy harmonization across multinational firms, acquired entities, and evolving business models.
Draft employee-facing policy communications, FAQs, and intranet content to support consistent understanding and application.

Training & Operational Excellence

jobs.title: Lead Data Analyst, Growth & Experimentation
jobs.description:
About LawnStarter

LawnStarter is the nation's leading on-demand marketplace for lawn care and outdoor services, with over $150M in annual bookings. We're expanding beyond lawn care into the one-stop shop for all home services. Getting there depends on how fast we can test, learn, and scale what works.

About The Data Team

We're a high-leverage team of Product Data Analysts embedded across the business, owning the semantic layer and the metrics everyone trusts. The experimentation program runs on real rigor, not vibes: pre-registered analysis plans gate every test launch, anytime-valid statistics keep mid-run dashboards honest under continuous viewing, automated daily SRM and attribution health sweeps catch broken tests early, and seasonal power forecasting accounts for a business that swings hard by time of year. The test lifecycle, design through readout, is already AI-driven. Our analysts are stretched across product, so Growth support has stayed part-time and reactive, until now.

The Role

You're the first data analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation. Your primary charter is the experimentation program
: test design, statistical rigor, and readouts across web funnels, SMS/drip, sales-driven tests, and SEO tests built on our own page-clustering tooling. It's a wider surface than most companies run. You also own the acquisition-to-conversion funnel
those tests move, across paid, organic, and partner channels. What to test and which direction to bet on is the CRO's and Growth PMs' call; you shape it, they decide it.

You're not starting from scratch. Dashboards, tooling, and rigor scaffolding are already shipped and running. Expect the early months to be hands-on and manual: scoping tests, crunching readouts, while you build toward a self-serve layer. If a test readout and a funnel refresh ever compete for your week, the test wins.

What Makes This Role Different

The CEO personally engages with test design here: real organizational weight, no fight for buy-in
You partner directly with the Director of CRO, performance marketing, and Growth PMs, who come to you when a test needs a call

Requirements

What You'll Own

Experimentation rigor: test design, power and sample-size calls, significance and readout standards. Core of the role: you catch underpowered tests and false positives before they become bad decisions, and you get Growth's tests onto the anytime-valid monitoring the program already runs, so early calls come from a crossed boundary instead of a hopeful trend read
The self-serve experimentation layer: automated Growth metrics in Lightdash, Python-backed stat-sig tooling, and the AI skills (Claude routines) already handling pre-test power calcs and live-test health checks. You extend these and keep the layer correct as product and tracking evolve
The Growth funnel model: a trusted, instrumented view of visitor → lead → customer across every brand and channel, with the CAC, LTV, and conversion-rate cuts Growth needs to prioritize investment
The Growth analytics function model: by end of Year 1, the standards and playbook that scale this function beyond one person, plus a buy-vs-build recommendation for the experimentation stack (an off-the-shelf stats engine, or extending our own skills and Python). You bring the recommendation; the final call isn't yours alone

Problems to Solve

Tests that can't answer the question they were run for
Growth wants more experiments, but volume without rigor produces confident, wrong conclusions. Raising the bar without becoming the bottleneck is the job.

Getting off the manual treadmill
Real tooling already exists: test-design helpers, dashboards, AI skills. Most tests are still hands-on and bespoke. How do you extend that automation so routine cases genuinely self-serve?

Making the funnel decision-grade
The semantic layer defines the funnel, but instrumentation is uneven across brands and channels, and no one owns the single trusted view. You build it, and you keep it trusted.

Turning analysis into decisions
The hard part isn't the SQL. It's getting a PM or marketer to change course. Can you deliver insight sharp enough that the room acts, and push back when the data favors the popular but wrong idea?

What Success Looks Like (Year 1)

Rigor is the default. Power calculations are standard practice, early stops on Growth tests come from the anytime-valid boundary rather than a trend read, and the re-run rate (redone for tracking or attribution problems) is down
Routine tests self-serve. Metrics and stat-sig are automated in Lightdash, so the team reads standard results without filing a ticket, and your time goes to the tests that need an analyst
A funnel Growth trusts. The acquisition→conversion funnel is instrumented across every brand and channel; Growth prioritizes off your model, not side spreadsheets
Measurable conversion wins. Your analysis directly drove specific, quantified lifts in the funnel, and you can name them

Who You Are

AI-native.
You use AI daily for SQL, dbt, and pressure-testing your analysis, extending the skills already running our experimentation process rather than merely using them. This is unlikely to be a good fit if you're skeptical of AI or treat your workflow as fixed.

A partner, not a report-writer.
You don't wait for a ticket. You sit close to Growth and bring the question before anyone asks it. Skip this one if you want a clear queue with no expectation to push back.

Statistically sharp.
Wrong fit if "we hit significance" ends your analysis instead of starting it. Right fit if you have a point of view on test design (power, significance, novelty and interaction effects, when not to test) and can explain a broken experiment in plain terms.

Fluent in experiment instrumentation.
You know how Segment events and Flagsmith randomization interact, and catch a tracking problem before a test ships, keeping our re-run rate down. This isn't for you if instrumentation is someone else's job.

Fluent in the funnel.
You think in CAC, LTV, and channel economics, and know acquisition data's quirks: attribution messiness, seasonality, channel mix. Skip this one if your background is pure product-feature analytics.

Technically self-sufficient.
Wrong fit if you need clean data handed to you. Expert SQL, enough Python to automate the stat-sig math, and comfort in dbt and Lightdash, building your own models without waiting on data engineering.

Influences without authority.
PMs and marketers act on what you find because your insight is clear and honest about uncertainty. This isn't for you if you consider the job done once the analysis ships, regardless of outcome.

This Role Is NOT

A ticket queue. Not the role if you want well-defined asks: no one hands you a backlog of number-pulls, you decide what's worth measuring
The person who decides what to test. You shape that call and own its rigor, but the roadmap and final direction belong to the CRO and Growth PMs
A product-feature analyst seat. Existing analysts already own product, pricing, and service delivery; this one lives in Growth: acquisition, conversion, experimentation
A pure platform or dashboard-builder. You'll automate metrics, stat-sig, and AI skills into a self-serve layer, but that's the means. The job is designing experiments and keeping that automation correct as product and tracking evolve
A people-management role. This is an individual-contributor seat

Benefits

Base salary: $75,000-$100,000 USD annually
The scope is the draw: First analyst dedicated entirely to Growth and Experimentation, with your fingerprints on how this company decides what works
AI tooling provided: The Claude routines already running pieces of our experimentation process are yours to extend, not a side project you have to justify
Fully remote: This is deep-focus analytical work with US-facing partners. We hire the best analyst regardless of city and trust you to manage your environment and overlap hours
Flexible PTO: Measured on outcomes, not hours logged

People Management & Team Development

Directly manage a team of Network Implementation Engineers across project delivery lifecycle; set clear performance expectations, conduct structured 1:1s, and own individual development plans.
Build a culture of execution discipline — ticket hygiene, change management compliance, documentation quality, and rigorous project close-out.
Identify skill gaps and build structured training and certification pathways aligned to ECI’s service portfolio.
Manage performance formally and informally; address issues directly, constructively, and on record when required.
Participate in hiring decisions for the implementation function, including technical assessments and structured panel interviews.

Project Delivery & Program Management

Own end-to-end delivery of network implementation projects spanning new client onboarding, infrastructure refreshes, office builds, and technology migrations.
Define and enforce project intake, scoping, scheduling, and resource allocation standards across the team.
Maintain active visibility across all open workstreams; surface and resolve blockers before they become client escalations.
Drive post-implementation reviews and root cause analysis; translate findings into repeatable process improvements for the team.
Coordinate with Client Services, Solutions Architecture, and pre-sales to align implementation timelines with client commitments and ECI delivery standards.

Technical Standards & Oversight

Serve as the technical authority for ECI’s implementation standards covering Cisco (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls, Meraki, and SD-WAN platforms.
Review and approve low-level designs (LLDs) and implementation runbooks before execution.
Establish and enforce configuration standards that ensure consistency, repeatability, and alignment with client security and compliance requirements (SOC 2, PCI-DSS, NIST, HIPAA).
Serve as escalation point for complex in-flight technical issues; engage hands-on when warranted while ensuring the team learns from every resolution.
Champion Zero Trust and SASE architecture principles within ECI’s implementation workflows.

Client & Stakeholder Communication

Own implementation status communication to client stakeholders; translate technical risk into clear business impact language.
Represent the implementation team in internal delivery reviews, capacity planning, and service improvement forums.
Maintain ECI’s documentation standard across implementation plans, network diagrams, as-built records, and configuration baselines — ensuring clean handoffs to managed services teams.

Qualifications

Required

10+ years of progressive network engineering experience with a demonstrable track record in enterprise implementation, ideally within an MSP or multi-client environment.
3+ years of direct people management — you have hired engineers, set goals, handled performance, and actively developed talent.
Deep technical proficiency in Cisco networking (Catalyst, Nexus, IOS-XE/XR), Palo Alto firewalls (App-ID, Threat Prevention, VPN, Panorama), and wireless (WLC, Meraki MR/MS/MX).
Strong working knowledge of routing protocols (BGP, OSPF, EIGRP), VLANs, QoS, and IPv4/IPv6 fundamentals.
Proven ability to run multiple concurrent implementation projects with accountability for schedules, resources, and stakeholder communication.
Solid understanding of security frameworks, compliance standards, and change management governance in regulated client environments.

Preferred

Active CCNP, CCIE, or PCNSE certification; equivalent demonstrated expertise considered.
Experience with SD-WAN (Cisco Viptela, VeloCloud) and SASE / Zero Trust architecture in client deployments.
Familiarity with automation tooling (Python, Ansible) to drive repeatability and reduce manual effort across the team.
Experience with network monitoring platforms (SolarWinds, PRTG, Meraki Insights) and using telemetry data to drive delivery quality.
Hedge fund, financial services, or similarly regulated client-facing environment experience is a strong plus.

Education

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field — or equivalent professional experience.

Who We Are Looking For

Beyond credentials, we are hiring for a specific leadership profile. The right candidate:

Communicates expectations without ambiguity and follows through consistently. Leads with clarity.
Engineers respect them because they know the stack — not just the title. Commands technical credibility.
Holds the team and themselves to high execution standards without micromanaging. Drives accountability.
Focused on delivery quality and reliability, not just activity volume. Solves for client outcomes.
Understands the job is to build the best team — not to be the best individual engineer on it. Scales through people.

ECI’s culture is all about connection -
connection with our clients, our technology and most importantly with each other. In addition to working with an amazing team around the world, ECI also offers a competitive compensation package and the range for this role is a maximum of $142,000 annually with flexible PTO, health benefit eligibility the first of the month, life insurance, pet insurance, 401K and so much more! The Accounting Systems & Operations Analyst will sit within DCG's accounting team and work across both accounting operations and financial systems. Curious and proactive, with a genuine interest in understanding how accounting processes, systems, and data work together.

We’re looking for someone who understands managed repair networks, keeps multiple jobs organized, and follows through with homeowners, subcontractors, and program representatives.

Proven experience managing multiple residential restoration or reconstruction projects through completion.

Experience with Xactimate, AccuLynx, estimating and supplements

The Sales and Inventory Analyst will play a key role in supporting sales operations through accurate forecasting, customer portal setup, sales and product analytics, and administrative support for the sales team. Strong analytical and financial skills with a deep understanding of inventory dynamics.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel (pivot tables, VLOOKUPs, data modeling); experience with ERP systems and BI tools a plus.

Excellent communication and organizational skills with a detail-oriented mindset.
Ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
Self-motivated with a strong sense of accountability and a focus on contributing to the bottom line.

Growing U.S. business with expanding distribution and increasing market presence
Long-term stability and leadership from a well-established Japanese parent company
Opportunity to own high-impact accounts and influence strategic growth initiatives
Collaborative, professional environment with a strong brand reputation in the pet industry

jobs.title: Senior Research Analyst
jobs.description:
Join Goodwin’s Global Operations Team, and make a real impact on a global scale.
At Goodwin, we work with some of the world’s most successful and innovative investors, entrepreneurs and disruptors in the life sciences, private equity, real estate, technology and financial industries, and where they converge. As part of the Global Operations Team – all business professionals at the firm – you’ll collaborate with colleagues from varied backgrounds and experiences, fostering an environment where cross-functional learning, networking, and collaboration are at the core of what we do.

Here, we’re not just supporting a law firm; we’re partnering with attorneys and clients to deliver cutting-edge solutions
in high-stakes litigation and dispute resolution, world-class regulatory compliance and advisory services, and complex transactions. Our commitment to integrity, ingenuity, agility, and ambition drives us, and we’re proud to have been recognised as the “Best Business Team” by The American Lawyer.

This is your opportunity to grow professionally in a dynamic, global environment, surrounded by forward-thinking peers.

The Senior Research Analyst conducts in-depth legal and business research to support the firm’s attorneys and administrative departments; engages in the firm’s educational initiatives by developing and delivering subject area specific training, develops and delivers appropriate on-boarding programming for new associates and offers consultative services on complex research projects. This role proactively monitors the legal industry and the latest developments in legal and business GenAI tools and strategizes with the Director of Research Services to implement solutions to advance the objectives of Research Services and the firm.

What You’ll Do

Delivers proactive and value-added research to the firm.
Provides expert legal and business research assistance to attorneys and administrative staff in a timely and effective manner, leveraging sophisticated research applications and incorporating new technologies as appropriate.
Maintains expert-level knowledge of internal knowledge management resources and systems to enhance research deliverables .
Provides analysis and synthesis of research results and presents findings in a manner promoting effective decision making where appropriate.
Advises attorneys on research strategy and resource selection to ensure research is accurate and conducted in the most efficient and cost effective manner.
Provides research coverage as assigned and follows established internal procedures for the handling of requests to ensure timely and efficient delivery of results.
Utilizes workflow software to assign and manage research projects.
Develops curriculum and conducts training to promote effective and authoritative research.
Creates and maintains newsletters and alerts using news aggregators.
Conducts new hire on-boarding for administrative and legal staff.
Contributes to the development and maintenance of the Research Services intranet.
Participates in the ongoing evaluation of online resources and makes recommendations for purchase or renewal.
Prioritizes continuous learning by seeking professional development opportunities.
Other duties as assigned.

Who You Are:  

Master of Library Science from an ALA accredited library school. Demonstrated, relevant professional research experience in a private law firm or academic law library, special library or research center can be substituted for the MLS.
7+ years’ experience providing research in a private law firm, academic law library or special library or research center.
Expert knowledge of a wide variety of information sources, such as Westlaw, Lexis, S&P Capital IQ, PitchBook, Intelligize, InfoNgen, Derwent Innovation, and Saegis.
Knowledge of emerging technologies, including data analytics and artificial intelligence and how those technologies impact research and the research process.
Employs research interview skills in order to clarify and interpret research requests.
Strong interpersonal, written and oral communication skills.
Ability to prioritize work, multitask and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to work independently, as well as collaboratively, with members of the team and Firm.
Demonstrated knowledge of computer applications, such as Excel, SharePoint, PowerPoint, and Zoom.

Benefits And More

At Goodwin, you will discover your next career opportunity with a rewarding compensation package and comprehensive benefits, including:

Health, dental, and vision insurance
Life and disability insurance
Retirement & Savings Plan
Emergency back-up child and adult care
Paid vacation, sick time off, and holidays
Professional development and career advancement opportunities
Employee recognition and reward programs
Employee wellness and assistance programs
Employee discounts and perks

This position is eligible for overtime: No

The Target Salary Range For This Position Varies By Location And Is Commensurate With Relevant Experience: $130,000.00 - $145,000.00

Transforming Life Science Consulting Worldwide.

Fusion Consulting is a globally leading Business and IT boutique consultancy specialized in the Life Sciences industry, partnering with leading companies in pharma, healthcare, and animal health.

With over 450 employees and 25 offices worldwide, our mission is to revolutionize our clients' business transformation challenges and set new industry standards through innovative solutions.

Focused on S/4HANA, Data & Cloud, and innovative technologies, Fusion Consulting brings unparalleled expertise and commitment to excellence to every project we undertake.

Grounded in our commitment to fast and intelligent decision-making, our client-first and open-hearted approach defines our ethos. With unwavering support and an entrepreneurial spirit, our global teamwork transcends boundaries and turns shared visions into reality.

At Fusion, we unite entrepreneurial minds from around the globe to develop and implement game-changing solutions that build lasting relationships with our clients.

Job Description

The Senior IT Project Manager is responsible for leading the end-to-end delivery of Salesforce transformation and optimization initiatives within the pharmaceutical industry. The role focuses on Salesforce org simplification, third-party system rationalization, and digital communication platform enhancements to support enterprise digital transformation. Working closely with business stakeholders, IT teams, vendors, and architects, the Project Manager ensures successful project execution, effective risk management, and the delivery of scalable, streamlined digital solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Lead end-to-end delivery of Salesforce transformation projects, including org simplification, system consolidation, and platform optimization initiatives.
Manage projects focused on simplifying Salesforce integrations with third-party applications and reducing application landscape complexity.
Drive continuous enhancement of digital communication platforms and related business capabilities.
Develop and manage project plans, schedules, budgets, resource allocation, risks, and dependencies.
Coordinate cross-functional teams across Business, IT, Salesforce, Architecture, and external vendors.
Facilitate stakeholder alignment, governance meetings, status reporting, and executive communications.
Ensure project deliverables meet quality standards and align with business, compliance, and technology objectives.
Support enterprise digital transformation by promoting standardized processes, scalable solutions, and improved system architecture.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum 5 years of experience managing enterprise IT projects, preferably within pharmaceutical, life sciences, or regulated industries.
Proven experience delivering Salesforce-related projects, including Salesforce CRM implementations, enhancements, or transformation initiatives.
Strong understanding of Salesforce multi-org architectures, integration patterns, and system simplification methodologies.
Experience managing third-party system integrations and application rationalization initiatives.
Basic understanding of enterprise digital communication platforms and related business processes.
Proficiency in Agile and Waterfall project management methodologies.
Strong stakeholder management, project governance, risk management, and communication skills.

You’ll work alongside experienced consultants on complex, meaningful projects that demand both precision and innovation. Our culture emphasizes continuous learning, open knowledge sharing, and cross-functional teamwork—empowering you to grow both professionally and personally.

Joining Fusion Means Becoming Part Of a Company That

Builds strong, trusted partnerships with clients, delivering tailored solutions that create real business value.
Drives delivery excellence, holding ourselves accountable for the quality and impact of every outcome.
Encourages entrepreneurial thinking, empowering you to take initiative, solve problems, and lead change.
Operates with a truly global mindset, where diverse perspectives, cultures, and collaboration fuel our success.

About Blooming Health

Blooming Health is on a mission to transform social care! Our AI-powered platform identifies social needs and barriers by continuously collecting real-time data from member interactions and screenings. It then drives action through automated, empathetic outreach in 55+ languages/dialects to engage individuals across voice, SMS, and email, and coordinating referrals to the right services at the right time. The result is improved access to care, higher program participation, and better outcomes across diverse populations. Our platform supports 1,000+ community organizations across the US, helping millions of members access the support they need to stay healthy. We don’t just offer software—we deliver impact.

About The Role

As we scale, we’re looking for a highly driven and technically sophisticated Senior Technical Program Manager to own delivery execution across Blooming Health’s Engineering, AI, and Product organizations. This is a US-based remote role with preference for working on EST or CST hours.

This Senior TPM will serve as the operational backbone of the product development organization, ensuring critical initiatives are delivered on time, dependencies are managed proactively, and leadership has complete visibility into roadmap progress, customer implementations, and organizational priorities. While Engineering and Product leaders define strategy, architecture, and roadmap direction, this role is responsible for driving execution, accountability, and delivery outcomes across the organization.

This is not a project coordinator or ticket-tracking role. We are looking for someone who can operate as a force multiplier for leadership—someone who understands complex technical systems, thrives in ambiguity, navigates competing priorities, and creates structure where none exists. The ideal candidate combines strong program management expertise, technical credibility, startup execution experience, and exceptional communication skills.

Engineering Delivery Leadership:
Own the end-to-end delivery process across Engineering, AI, and Product teams. Drive sprint planning, backlog management, dependency tracking, roadmap execution, and delivery accountability across multiple concurrent initiatives.

Program Execution & Accountability:
Establish and enforce operating rhythms, delivery processes, and accountability frameworks that ensure teams consistently meet commitments and execution risks are surfaced early.

Cross-Functional Coordination:
Partner closely with Engineering, AI, Product, Customer Success, and Implementation teams to align priorities, manage dependencies, and ensure critical information flows effectively across the organization.

Customer Deployment Oversight:
Coordinate delivery across multiple concurrent customer implementations, balancing customer commitments, product priorities, and engineering capacity while proactively identifying risks and resource conflicts.

Risk Management & Escalation:
Identify blockers, timeline risks, resource constraints, and delivery challenges before they become critical issues. Facilitate decision-making and drive resolution across teams and stakeholders.

Executive Reporting & Visibility:
Serve as the central source of truth for delivery status across the organization. Provide clear, concise, executive-ready updates on roadmap progress, customer deployments, risks, dependencies, and organizational priorities.

Technical Program Leadership:
Participate in technical discussions and architecture reviews to understand delivery implications, identify dependencies, and support informed prioritization decisions across complex systems.

Process Design & Continuous Improvement:
Build scalable program management processes that improve organizational effectiveness without creating unnecessary bureaucracy. Continuously evolve delivery frameworks as the company grows and product complexity increases.

What We're Looking For

Requirements

Technical Program Management Expertise: 10+ years of experience in Technical Program Management, Engineering Program Management, Product Operations, Engineering Operations, or related delivery-focused leadership roles.
Startup & Growth-Stage Experience: Proven success operating within fast-paced startup environments, ideally helping organizations scale from early product-market fit through rapid customer growth and organizational expansion.
Complex Technical Delivery Experience: Demonstrated experience managing technically sophisticated initiatives involving distributed systems, AI/ML platforms, cloud-native architectures, customer-facing products, or other highly complex software environments.
AI/ML or Agentic Systems Experience: Experience supporting AI, machine learning, agentic systems, or similarly complex and iterative technology development environments where delivery timelines and success metrics are less deterministic than traditional software development.
Strong SDLC & Program Management Foundations: Deep understanding of Agile, Scrum, Kanban, and modern software development lifecycle practices. Ability to apply process thoughtfully based on organizational needs rather than rigid adherence to methodology.
Technical Credibility: Comfortable participating in discussions involving architecture, infrastructure, system design, APIs, data flows, cloud platforms, and engineering tradeoffs. Able to understand delivery implications of technical decisions without serving as the technical decision-maker.

Self-Starter Mentality: Highly proactive and capable of establishing structure, processes, and operating rhythms in ambiguous environments with limited guidance.

If you're passionate about leveraging technology to provide the best customer service experience and are ready to be a part of our journey, we welcome you to explore opportunities at Swyfft!

About the Position:

We are looking for a strategic, tech-minded Project Manager to lead the planning and execution of key initiatives across the company. You'll work across multiple systems, vendors, and teams, and will be relied on to prioritize, organize, and wrangle competing processes, workflows, and technical requirements. All of which will need to be documented along the way (but you're a PM so you already know that).

Swyfft's business runs across three core lifecycle phases — Pre-Bind, Post-Bind, and Claims — each with its own teams, systems, and cadence. Work-life balance

new_jobs.title: Program Manager, Product Management

The Program Manager provides Product Management leadership with a single, trustworthy view of progress on the organization's strategic, large-scale initiatives.
Examples include: product modernization, AI, and other transformational projects across a portfolio of 40+ industry-specific software products. Working at the intersection of product, engineering, and leadership, the Program Manager owns accurate status reporting, milestone tracking, and risk visibility for these key projects, translating complex project details into clear, decision-ready reporting for executives and stakeholders.

This is a highly visible, cross-functional role that succeeds through influence, disciplined communication, and data rather than direct authority. The Program Manager works directly with product owners and cross-functional project teams to keep high-stakes initiatives on track, and gives leadership a real-time, honest picture of progress across the organization's most important product bets.

What You'll Do

Manage and Report on Key Strategic Initiatives

Manage and support key large-scale product projects. Actively manage progress on the organization's strategic product initiatives including product modernization, AI/ML integration, and other transformational, multi-quarter projects as examples, partnering closely with product owners and project teams to keep work moving against plan.
Own status reporting to leadership. Build and maintain accurate, timely, executive-ready status reports and dashboards for key projects, giving leadership a clear, consolidated view of progress, milestones, budget/resourcing status, and delivery timelines across the portfolio.
Track project health and key metrics. Define and monitor the milestones, KPIs, and success metrics for each large-scale initiative, translating detailed project activity into concise, decision-ready insight for leadership and flagging projects that are off track.

Keep Initiatives On Track

Identify and escalate risks and issues. Proactively identify risks, issues, blockers, and cross-team dependencies threatening a project's scope, schedule, or quality; maintain a clear view of open items and escalate to leadership with recommended paths forward.
Run project governance and cadence. Establish and facilitate a regular cadence of project reviews and checkpoints with project teams and leadership ensuring each key initiative has a consistent forum for reporting progress, making decisions, and resolving blockers.
Drive accountability across project teams. Hold project owners and cross-functional contributors (engineering, design, product marketing, product management, sales, customer success) accountable to committed timelines and deliverables, following up on action items and unresolved issues between checkpoints.

Communicate and Support Decision-Making

Communicate with stakeholders. Tailor communication of project status and impact for different audiences, from individual project teams to senior executives, keeping stakeholders informed and aligned throughout each initiative's lifecycle.
Support prioritization and planning. Provide leadership with the visibility needed to make informed trade-off and sequencing decisions across the portfolio of large-scale initiatives, based on current progress, risk, and resourcing.

Who You'll Work With

Product Management, Engineering, Design, Product Marketing, Sales, and Customer Success, as well as the Product leadership team. You will be the connective tissue that turns complex project details into consistent, decision-ready reporting, and an honest, real-time picture of how the organization's most important initiatives are performing.

Qualifications

Required

Bachelor's degree in Business, Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3–5 years of program or project management experience.
Demonstrated experience managing and reporting on the progress of strategic projects from initiation through delivery.
Hands-on proficiency using AI tools for program management and reporting.
Utilization and integration of AI in daily workflows.
Proven ability to build clear, accurate, executive-level status reports and dashboards and to present project progress confidently to senior leadership.
Experience identifying, tracking, and escalating project risks, issues, and dependencies, and driving resolution with cross-functional teams.
Experience establishing and running project governance cadences (e.g., steering committees, project reviews, checkpoint meetings).

Preferred

PMP certification; PgMP.
Experience managing large-scale, complex, or transformational initiatives in a software/SaaS or technology environment.
Experience in a large, multi-product software organization or a portfolio shaped by mergers and acquisitions, where products operate with a high degree of autonomy.
Familiarity with ERP or vertical-market/industry-specific software.
Experience working within or alongside a Product Management organization with product roadmaps and release processes.
Experience presenting project updates to senior executive audiences.

How Success Is Measured

Performance is measured on a paired set of leading and outcome indicators across the role:

Reporting reliability. Timeliness, accuracy, and leadership-rated trustworthiness of status reporting and dashboards for key strategic initiatives.
Risk visibility. Early identification and escalation of risks and issues — measured by how often problems are surfaced in time for leadership to act, rather than discovered after the fact.
Initiative outcomes. On-time, on-track support of the organization's key modernization, AI, and other large-scale product projects, and leadership-rated confidence in the governance cadence.

new_jobs.title: Technical Program Manager
Program Manager II, El Nino Preparedness South America – EMPOWER/RAPID
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Program Manager II will provide time-bound program management, technical support, accompaniment, and training to EMPOWER partners in South America to strengthen El Niño preparedness and readiness for rapid, partner-led emergency response. The position will coordinate preparedness programming across priority countries and hotspots, translating hazard, vulnerability, market, operational, and partner-capacity analysis into practical readiness actions, quality program designs, and activation-ready response plans.

Working closely with the Supply Chain Management Technical Advisor II and other technical and operational colleagues, the Program Manager II will align program strategies, targeting, transfer modalities, technical standards, MEAL, accountability, safeguarding, protection, and partner capacity strengthening with sourcing, contracting, logistics, cash and voucher assistance, and distribution readiness. The role will help partners identify and close priority program bottlenecks, test readiness arrangements, and maintain an integrated package that can be rapidly adapted when an EMPOWER/RAPID response is activated.

Roles And Key Responsibilities

Lead the programmatic El Niño preparedness process across South America priority countries in close coordination with EMPOWER partners, country program or program office teams, RAPID counterparts, technical advisors, MEAL, and supply chain and operations colleagues.
Develop and maintain an integrated assignment workplan and deliverable calendar that links program, MEAL, partnership, cash and voucher assistance, supply chain, finance, safeguarding, and operational readiness activities.
Coordinate hazard, vulnerability, exposure, seasonal, and scenario analysis to identify priority countries, hotspots, population groups, likely needs, access constraints, and preparedness triggers for drought, floods, food insecurity, wildfires and related El Niño impacts.
Lead stakeholder and service mapping with partners, including government authorities, Caritas structures, humanitarian coordination bodies, community actors, technical services, financial service providers, and other response stakeholders.
Support partners to develop or update country- and hotspot-specific contingency plans, response strategies, sector and modality options, targeting approaches, geographic priorities, and scalable response scenarios.
Work with sector technical leads and partners to define minimum program quality standards, intervention packages, eligibility and prioritization criteria, transfer values or assistance quantities, referral pathways, and safe adaptation or substitution rules.
Coordinate with the Supply Chain Management Technical Advisor II to validate proposed relief kits, in-kind assistance, and cash or voucher options against assessed needs, local market capacity, cultural appropriateness, protection considerations, delivery feasibility, lead times, and cost drivers.
Integrate market and logistics findings into program design, including modality selection, remote-area feasibility, delivery sequencing, contingency options, and realistic procurement and implementation timelines.
Support partner readiness for cash and voucher assistance by defining program requirements for geographic coverage, transfer modalities, participant data, accountability, complaints handling, protection, inclusion, reconciliation, monitoring, and failed-payment follow-up in coordination with operations and finance teams.
Lead development of activation-ready program packages, including concise needs assessment tools, rapid response concepts, targeting and registration approaches, implementation plans, staffing assumptions, budgets, procurement inputs, risk assessments, and donor-ready narrative components.
Provide management, guidance, and technical oversight throughout preparedness and any activated response cycle so that design, start-up, implementation, monitoring, adaptation, and close-out align with CRS program quality principles and standards, donor requirements, and humanitarian best practice.
Collaborate with MEAL and information management colleagues to establish preparedness indicators where feasible, baseline or reference data, data-collection and analysis tools, monitoring plans, feedback and response mechanisms, and learning questions.
Ensure that safeguarding, protection mainstreaming, gender, age, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations, conflict sensitivity, and disaster risk reduction are integrated across assessments, designs, partner tools, simulations, and readiness plans.
Assess partner program-management and technical readiness; facilitate participatory prioritization and partner-specific action plans with clear actions, responsible persons, deadlines, support needs, approvals, risks, contingencies, escalation points, and maintenance responsibilities.
Design and facilitate coaching, working sessions, simulations, tabletop exercises, or readiness tests so partner teams can practice assessment, decision-making, coordination, modality selection, activation, implementation, monitoring, adaptation, and reporting.
Contribute to partner capacity strengthening through tailored learning strategies, agendas and curricula, workshops, mentoring, and coaching based on priorities identified by partners.
Support quality donor engagement and resource mobilization by contributing technical analysis, program design, proposal writing, budgeting, staffing plans, and donor discussions for El Niño preparedness and rapid response opportunities.
Promote strong, equitable partnerships in line with CRS and Caritas Internationalis partnership principles and facilitate timely resolution of programmatic or coordination challenges through dialogue and appropriate support.
Contribute to knowledge management by documenting decisions, lessons, tested approaches, readiness gaps, good practices, and recommendations that can inform EMPOWER/RAPID programming in South America and other regions.
Consolidate and hand over the final El Niño program preparedness package, including analyses, contingency and response plans, assessment and design tools, MEAL materials, partner action plans, training resources, ownership arrangements, maintenance recommendations, and an exit debrief.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Strong program management and technical skills across emergency preparedness, rapid needs assessment, response design, contingency planning, implementation, monitoring, adaptation, and close-out.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to synthesize hazard, vulnerability, market, operational, and partner information into prioritized, realistic actions.
Good grants management and budgeting experience, including design and proposal development for public or institutional donors.
MEAL and information-management skills, including development of practical indicators, data-collection tools, analysis approaches, feedback mechanisms, and reporting products. Experience with KoboToolbox, CommCare, or similar tools is desirable.
Ability to facilitate partner-led processes, build trust, adapt technical support to partner priorities, and promote sustainable ownership of preparedness systems.
Excellent planning, coordination, documentation, facilitation, presentation, and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and deliverables across countries.
Strong relationship-management and professional communication skills, with the ability to work effectively with partner leadership, technical teams, donors, government, and internal support functions.
Proactive, resourceful, culturally sensitive, solution-oriented, and results-focused.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, web-conferencing platforms, and common information-management systems.

Required Languages:
Professional fluency in English and Spanish is required. Professional proficiency in Portuguese is strongly preferred; French is an advantage for engagement across target regions.

Travel:
The assignment will be primarily remote, with in-country or regional travel to priority partners, countries, or hotspots as approved and operationally required. The selected candidate must be willing and able to travel up to 50 percent within South America and work effectively across time zones and in diverse operating environments.

Supervisory Responsibility:
No

Qualifications

Basic Qualifications

Proven ability to lead through influence, facilitate cross-functional decision-making, and drive accountability for deliverables
Proficiency in interpreting and analyzing healthcare data from dashboards and reports (e.g., Tableau, Power BI, Excel, or similar tools)
Advanced Excel functions for manipulating, analyzing, and visualizing population and claims data to inform data-driven decision-making and actionable recommendations
Experience in program evaluation, cost analysis, and identifying trends in healthcare utilization
Strong leadership and team management skills with the ability to oversee large-scale initiatives
Excellent project management skills, including experience with Agile methodologies and performance tracking
Proven ability to build and maintain relationships with healthcare providers, community organizations, and government agencies
Effective communication and executive presentation skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable insights
Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills; ability to synthesize complex data into clear insights and actionable recommendations
Experience with quality improvement methodologies and other process optimization frameworks

Experience developing policies/procedures, facilitating governance forums, or managing vendors/contracts
Ability to work effectively with diverse individuals and groups
Ability to learn, focus, understand, and evaluate information and determine appropriate actions

Ability to hear and speak clearly for at least 3-6 hours/day

new_jobs.title: Program Manager Lead
new_jobs.description:
At GFiber, we believe that great internet has the power to drive innovation, strengthen communities, enable the impossible, and do all the everyday things that make all of our world go round. And the job of creating better internet is never done - so we’re growing! Our team is committed to building a place where people who want to make a difference can grow their careers and find their spot to belong.

GFiber is an Alphabet company that brings Google Fiber and Google Fiber Webpass internet services to homes and businesses across the United States. Our teams are expanding as we connect more cities and people to exceptional internet.

The application window will be open until at least September 14th, 2026
. This opportunity will remain online based on business needs which may be before or after the specified date.

This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship.

Role Description:

The PgM Lead will manage a team of program managers to ensure schedules are met and critical projects are delivered. These projects will span engineering, operations, construction, budgets, forecasting and planning. The PgM Lead is tasked with ensuring the team executes against strategic priorities set by leadership. The ideal candidate mixes tenacity, organizational skills, strong communication and leadership. This role requires prioritizing tasks, managing a complex schedule, ensuring deliverables are met across multiple work streams and being an effective cross functional leader. The PgM Lead works across the organization to refine and evolve our projects, as well as deploy new technologies to markets and communities throughout the market(s).

In this role you’ll:

Management functions to include aspects of project initiation, planning, executing, controlling, and closing.
Operate across internal Google Fiber groups and external organizations to ready and implement operational processes.
Lead process improvements that result in efficiency and efficacy gains throughout deployment and operations in the market(s).
Execute multiple projects/programs/planning in support of long term success
Manage full time employees and delivery of projects through strategic partners/vendors.

At a minimum, we would like you to have:

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, Telecommunications or a closely related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Proven experience in successfully managing a complex schedule with a diverse vendor base, leading annual planning cycles, developing and managing contracts, invoicing, budgeting, forecasting, project reporting (costs, status and risks), procurement and negotiating with vendors.
10 years of leadership experience in Telecommunications, Consulting, Oil and Gas or other capital project related industries.
5 years of people (direct report responsibilities for FTEs, performance evaluations, career management, etc) and/or vendor management (RFx, contract negotiations, scope management, etc).
Travel - up to 25%

It’s preferred if you have:

PMP certification, MBA, or advanced degree.
5 years of experience with fiber network deployments, including experience with constructing new outside and inside plant fiber infrastructure, and 5 years of experience with FTTH infrastructure.
Familiar with GIS (Geographic Information Systems) and database management including AutoCAD, ESRI, and/or shape file functionality.
Knowledge of network drawings, route maps and scopes of work and interpreting fiber test results and auditing projects for compliance with scopes of work.
Experience in operational improvement and process/workflow development.
Excellent analytical, financial skills and communication skills.

The US base salary range for this full-time position is between $136,000 - $149,600 + bonus + benefits. As pay varies by location, your recruiter will share more about the specific salary range for your targeted location during the hiring process.

Thales people architect identity management and data protection solutions at the heart of digital security. Business and governments rely on us to bring trust to the billions of digital interactions they have with people. Our technologies and services help banks exchange funds, people cross borders, energy become smarter and much more. More than 30,000 organizations already rely on us to verify the identities of people and things, grant access to digital services, analyze vast quantities of information and encrypt data to make the connected world more secure.

Position Summary

Austin, Hybrid

As a Technical Project Manager
for the Identity and Biometrics Solutions team, you will deliver solutions that meet external customer requirements and Thales’ commitments.

The Technical Project Manager manages and coordinates internal (Control Account Managers, Work Package Managers, developers, engineers, etc.) and external (customers, suppliers, sub-contractors, partners, etc.) dedicated teams by involving the following associated teams: Sales, finance, contract management, etc.

In this role, you will direct the project activities (including those relating to risks & opportunities) to ensure projects are delivered on-time, within budget, satisfy technical requirements, and meet customer expectations. This responsibility is exercised from signature of the contract through to the project completion period in terms of organization, time frame, workload, budget, etc.

The Identity and Biometrics Solutions team is responsible for the design and development of highly innovative components and products, from desktop applications integrating various hardware (biometric devices integration) to high performance server applications, including issuance of official documents in a very secure environment (PKI, encryption, cryptography), and leading the transformation to Digital Driver’s Licenses.

Regulatory Compliance Requirements

Must have U.S. Citizenship in order to obtain the post-hire Criminal Justice Information Services (CJIS) Clearance from the Federal Bureau of Investigation and must be able to obtain post-hire clearance from the Committee on Foreign Investments in the U.S. (CFIUS) and Department of Justice.

Key Areas of Responsibility

Establish and update project requirements baseline in a collaborative work with the Bid Manager and the Capture Leader
Establish and update project execution baseline (project structure, work package description, partners and supplier contractual data, management plans, costs, budgets and financial structure, resourced schedule, risks and mitigations)
Lead customer interactions for the project
Lead the project launch review and involves all stakeholders: project team, Management Plan and associated documents (WBS, OBS, schedule, budget allocations…), industrial scenario, project charter, team charter
Manage legal and contractual requirements including handling disputes

Close the project (archiving of documents, closing of the expenditure authorizations) by capitalizing and sharing onenterprise experience (lessons learnt)

Present monthly project dash board with project financials, project KPIs like variance and contingencies
Drive the project to ensure customer satisfaction by meeting deadlines, quality specifications, and project profitability
Build project schedule and cost baseline and update project forecast regularly (at-least every month)
Work closely with the PM Team Manager, Engineering, IT, Security and Operations ensuring clear communication, business based prioritization, and definition of precise scope and planning
Cultivate and maintain strong partnerships with decision-makers across operations groups (PMO, Procurement, Supply Chain, Data Center, Quality, Software Development and Validation, Manufacturing, Logistics and Ops Finance) to build and continuously improve process to ensure high quality and on-time delivery
Must ensure compliance of Thales, Customer, Security and all applicable regulations individually and for the project(s)

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science or similar field
PMP certification with 5 years of experience in technical/ engineering project management
Prior experience communicating pertinent and technical information to external customers and other stakeholders on a regular basis
Prior experience managing scope and requirements autonomously
Proven experience with PM tools – Confluence, JIRA or equivalent, building project schedules with Microsoft Project, and performing risk management activities such as project cost forecasting, measurement of project cost variance, developing and monitoring project risk contingencies and adherence to KPI’s
Proven track record with change management- planning for the various stages of transformational, transitional change, recognizing how people react to it and how it affects the organization
Technical understanding of multi-tier enterprise solution in a complex environment using software development (SDLC) - within Thales that translates to: front end, back end, data centers, deployment across locations, hardware deployment, software issues, network to and from locations, and disaster recovery –which are all part of the project

new_jobs.description:
Senior Engineering Program Manager

Role Overview
We are seeking an experienced Senior Engineering Program Manager (Sr. EPM)
to lead complex, cross-functional engineering programs from concept through delivery. This role partners closely with Engineering, Product Management, Architecture, Operations, Quality, and other business functions to translate strategic objectives into executable plans and drive predictable, high-quality outcomes.

The ideal candidate combines strong technical understanding with exceptional program leadership. You will operate effectively in ambiguous environments, identify dependencies and risks early, facilitate technical and business decisions, and provide clear visibility to senior leadership.

Key Responsibilities
Lead end-to-end execution of large, technically complex engineering programs involving multiple teams and workstreams.
Develop and maintain integrated program plans, roadmaps, milestones, schedules, dependencies, and critical paths.
Partner with engineering and product leaders to define program scope, requirements, priorities, deliverables, and success criteria.
Drive cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Product, Architecture, Operations, Quality, Security, and other stakeholder organizations.
Identify technical, schedule, resource, and organizational risks early and drive mitigation and contingency plans.
Facilitate technical reviews, requirements discussions, planning sessions, program reviews, and executive decision-making.
Track execution against commitments and proactively resolve blockers, dependencies, and conflicting priorities.
Establish effective program governance, operating rhythms, status reporting, escalation mechanisms, and decision frameworks.
Translate complex engineering issues into clear business impacts, options, trade-offs, and recommendations.
Provide concise program updates to directors, VPs, and executive stakeholders.
Partner with engineering leadership on resource planning, capacity constraints, sequencing, and prioritization.
Define and monitor program KPIs covering schedule, quality, execution, readiness, risk, and business outcomes.
Drive launch/readiness activities and ensure appropriate validation, operational readiness, and stakeholder sign-offs.
Lead retrospectives and implement improvements to engineering planning and execution processes.

new_jobs.title: Security Operations Manager
new_jobs.description:
Who We Are 🌍

We're IAG Loyalty - one organisation creating more rewarding ways to travel. Home to Avios, the global loyalty currency, we help millions of members collect and spend rewards across travel, retail and financial services.

We're transforming our technology landscape, investing in modern platforms and strengthening our cyber security capability to support our ambitious growth plans. It's an exciting time to join us as we continue to build a resilient, secure and customer-focused business.

The opportunity ✨

We're looking for a Security Operations Manager to play a key role in developing and maturing our Security Operations capability.

Working at the heart of our Cyber Security team, you'll act as the bridge between Security Engineering and Security Operations across IAG Group and our operating companies. You'll combine technical expertise with operational leadership to improve monitoring, strengthen threat detection, optimise security tooling and lead the response to security incidents.

This is a hands-on role where you'll have genuine influence over how Security Operations evolves. You'll shape the roadmap, improve operational resilience and ensure our security capabilities continue to develop as our technology landscape grows.

If you're passionate about building better security operations, enjoy solving complex technical challenges and want to make a visible impact, we'd love to hear from you.

What You'll Be Doing 🚀

You'll lead the continual improvement of our Security Operations capability, working closely with Security Engineering, technology teams and third-party partners to strengthen monitoring, detection and incident response across the business.

You'll own the end-to-end incident management lifecycle, coordinating responses to security incidents, driving investigations, facilitating lessons learned and ensuring improvement actions are delivered. Alongside this, you'll configure and optimise SIEM, threat protection and case management platforms, developing new detection rules, alerts and automation to improve our ability to identify and respond to emerging threats.

You'll build and maintain operational playbooks and runbooks, helping establish consistent ways of working across internal teams and managed service providers. You'll also produce meaningful KPIs and reporting, using operational data to identify trends, improve service performance and demonstrate the effectiveness of our security controls.

Working collaboratively across technology, engineering and business teams, you'll support security testing, assurance activities and resilience exercises, helping ensure our operational security capability continues to evolve in line with business priorities and regulatory expectations.

What We Need From You ⚡

Strong experience working within Security Operations, Cyber Defence or Incident Response in a complex enterprise environment
Proven experience managing the end-to-end security incident management lifecycle
Hands-on experience configuring and administering SIEM, threat protection, logging and case management platforms
Experience developing threat detection use cases, alerts, dashboards and operational reporting
Strong understanding of security monitoring, investigation, triage, containment, recovery and continuous improvement
Experience developing operational playbooks, runbooks and standard operating procedures
Experience working closely with Security Engineering teams to improve operational capabilities
Ability to collaborate with suppliers, technology teams and stakeholders across the business
Experience developing KPIs, operational reporting and service metrics
Strong analytical and communication skills, with the ability to translate technical information for different audiences
Good understanding of security governance, operational resilience and regulatory requirements

Desirable

Experience supporting Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery activities
Experience working with outsourced Security Operations Centres or Managed Security Service Providers
Familiarity with Microsoft Sentinel, Splunk, Microsoft Defender, CrowdStrike or similar enterprise security platforms
Experience automating security operations using scripting or SOAR technologies

We might not be right for you if...

You prefer working within a narrow technical specialism rather than owning security operations end-to-end.
You enjoy maintaining existing processes more than improving and evolving them.
You prefer working independently rather than collaborating across engineering, operations and business teams.

If you think you have what it takes but don't meet every single requirement, we'd still love to hear from you.

The Blend 📍

This role will work as part of our Loyalty Division and is based from our London office.

We call our approach to hybrid working The Blend — it's about giving you the flexibility to choose where you do your best work while staying connected with your team and the wider business.

You'll typically spend at least two days each week in the office, with the remainder working remotely. There may also be occasions where you'll work from other IAG or partner locations depending on business needs.

Diversity and Inclusion

Our vision is to create a more rewarding world of travel and experiences. Delivering that requires diverse thinking and inclusive leadership.

We are committed to building a workplace where people feel they belong and are valued for their perspective. Inclusion drives better decisions, stronger performance and more innovative outcomes.

We actively encourage applications from people with different experiences and backgrounds, and are committed to ensuring our recruitment process is fair, inclusive and accessible.

If you are passionate about cyber security and eager to make an impact, this role offers an exciting platform to develop your leadership expertise and to help to grow and mature a threat intelligence function in a critical national infrastructure provider.

Role

Lead the day-to-day operations of the threat intelligence function within the Vocalink Security Operations Centre, setting the strategy for proactive monitoring and alerting to help protect Vocalink assets and identify emerging threats.

Deliver briefings and regular engagements with our customers and partners across the business.

Prepare and QC intelligence reports for teams across the wider security function, including the SOC, Identity and Access Management, Vulnerability Management, Insider Threat and Physical Security, highlighting emerging threats and critical vulnerabilities.

Collaborate with Mastercard’s global threat intelligence team, supporting services that leverage Mastercard’s scale and capabilities.

Optimise reporting through our threat intelligence platform by working with vendors and internal teams to deliver high quality curated feeds which enable effective threat hunting and remediation.

Engage with vendors, industry groups, and government partners to build and maintain strong intelligence-sharing relationships.

Communicate findings clearly and promptly to internal stakeholders, ensuring accuracy and completeness.

Maintain and improve intelligence tooling, working with vendors and users to ensure the tools operate effectively.

Drive the growth and maturing of the threat intelligence function, developing new products and services for our internal and external customers.

All About You

An advanced knowledge of cyber threat intelligence and the intelligence lifecycle, with a deep understanding of all-source intelligence principles.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English, with the ability to present complex information clearly and concisely, including to senior audiences and under pressure.

A detailed understanding of attacker tools, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) and how they relate to threat actor behaviour.

A highly developed understanding of the current cyber threat landscape, including common threat actors, campaigns, and attack methodologies.

A strong understanding of key threat intelligence terminology, concepts, and analytical approaches.

Experience in analysis of dark and deep web ecosystems, including forums, leak sites, and threat actor communities.

To be adaptable and eager to learn new technologies, tools, and methodologies in a fast-paced environment.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and accuracy.

Strong technical proficiency, including familiarity with networking concepts, operating systems, and common security tools.

An interest in continuous professional development, including pursuing relevant certifications.

A developed understanding of geopolitical factors that impact and drive cyber risks.

A working understanding of financial market infrastructure.

Desirable Experience

Exposure to threat hunting activities and familiarity with investigative techniques.

A good understanding or hands-on experience with malware analysis and related tools.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
